description: The fern that carpets the rain forest floor: big evergreen clumps of stiff, arching, dark-green fronds, each 0.6-1.5 m long and lined with narrow, toothed leaflets that each carry a small 'hilt' at the base. Old fronds lie brown under the living ring and new fiddleheads uncurl in spring.

season_notes.winter: Evergreen; the fronds flatten under snow and spring back.
season_notes.spring: Silvery-scaled fiddleheads uncurl in April and May in a ring at the clump's centre.
season_notes.summer: Round brown spore dots in rows on the backs of the upper leaflets.
season_notes.fall: The oldest fronds wither and lie down around the clump; the living ones stay for several years.

notes: Drawn as a forb, the only ground form that has leaves of a shape: the 'rosette' habit with 'ferny' leaves (redstem filaree's, the template), sized up to 0.7 m, reads closest to a fern clump, the fronds rising from the base and spreading up and out, from above a star of fronds. The 'mound' habit was rejected because it scatters leaves through a dome, so fronds would start in mid-air. What a fern habit would need in forbs.js: (1) fronds from one central crown, each a curved rachis that rises steeply and arches over at the tip (sword fern) or lies out flat (deer fern sterile fronds); (2) pinnae many (30-50 a side) and narrow (about a tenth of the frond's length), tapering to the tip, against the ferny leaf's 5-7 broad lobes; (3) a ring structure: new fronds upright in the centre, older ones lower and outer, last years' dead ones brown on the ground (a dead_rgb ring, not the whole plant); (4) fiddleheads in April-May as coils at the centre; (5) a size large enough for a 1.5 m frond: the forb picture box is height_m[1] tall by 1.7 times that wide, so the frond length is capped near 0.7 m of a 1.2 m box; and (6) a far tier: sword fern covers whole hillsides here, but forbs draw only within 45 m, so the floor beyond would need the shrub impostors or a ground tint. Fronds 20-250 cm, over 1 m where it dominates, 75-100 fronds in a clump, evergreen for several years (FEIS). Note that forbs.js keeps only the first 16 forb species of the library (FORB_SPECIES, GS_MAX 16) and 19 forbs already exist, so this record will not draw until that limit is raised or made per tile. Roosevelt elk and black-tailed deer eat it in winter and mountain beavers depend on it (drafter's knowledge; the part of FEIS read did not cover wildlife); only the deer is in the animal library.
